own_solution.law: Newton's second law and rotational dynamics give T_L-3g=3a, 5g-T_R=5a, and (T_R-T_L)r=I(a/r). Consequently a=19.6/(8+I/r²) m/s². The pulley mass does not determine I/r², so there is no unique numerical answer.
assumptions: The string is taut and inextensible.
The pulley rotates about a fixed, frictionless axle.
The stated no-slip condition gives angular acceleration a/r.

T3426.regime: The string remains intact when both strand tensions are at most 200 N. For this ideal apparatus with nonnegative pulley inertia, neither tension exceeds 49 N.

TB300.regime: The string remains intact when both strand tensions are at most 200 N. For this ideal apparatus with nonnegative pulley inertia, neither tension exceeds 49 N.

uncertain_fields: Unconditional C classification of T3BAA and TF030 requires a specified pulley mass-distribution model.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The pulley mass is specified, but its moment of inertia or mass-distribution model is omitted, and different standard pulley models yield materially different accelerations.

counterexamples: A uniform solid-disk pulley has I/r²=1 kg and gives a=19.6/9=2.17778 m/s²; a thin-hoop pulley of the same mass and radius has I/r²=2 kg and gives a=19.6/10=1.96 m/s².
With either attached-block sentence, a=11.76/(8.8+I/r²) m/s²: the solid-disk model gives 1.20 m/s², whereas the thin-hoop model gives 1.08889 m/s².
notes: Null answers indicate underdetermination, not zero acceleration. The radius sentences are provisionally classified C under a fixed pulley shape factor κ, for which I=κMr² and radius cancels; specifying radius alone does not supply κ. Under the additional uniform solid-disk assumption, all sentences except T59AF and T5F33 retain the base answer 2.17778 m/s²; those two give 1.20 m/s². The sentence variants consistently use 0.8 kg, 200 N, and 12 cm, with no contradictory values. No outside information was accessed.
